mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which lowers discount rates and increases liquidity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly federal funds rate increase exceeding 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing immediate market repricing and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5 in one month).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and rise in payrolls indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer spending (RSAFS > 700,000 million) and strong housing starts (HOUST > 1,300 thousand) indicate robust demand, supporting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days in late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting the regime condition (RSAFS > 700000 and HOUST > 1300).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO above 100) indicates expanding manufacturing output, supporting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising (month-over-month).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1,200 thousand units signals weakening housing demand, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1200.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 325) with accommodative policy (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) leads to delayed rate cuts, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as investors anticipate persistent inflation.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the regime condition (CPIAUCSL > 325 and FEDFUNDS < 4.5).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate above 4.5% signals economic weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5.
